Lego Finder

1. Connect the arm (optional for now). 2. Turn the camera on with no Legos in view. 3. Put Legos down.
Fills the whole picture (no black bars). Zoom in until the Legos' play area fills the view. Hold the phone sideways for the widest view.

Arm: sort & inventory

Pass 1: red, orange, yellow, green, blue onto their piles; the others stay put. Pass 2: out of the others, the whites, then the light greys and dark greys onto their piles. Black and brown are never needed: they aren't shown and stay on the floor (a piece that might be dark grey is always kept as dark grey).
Connect the arm and turn the camera on. Calibrate once each time the phone or the arm is moved.

Settings

Anything smaller is ignored (carpet bits). Slide it and a square shows the size on the picture: make it a bit smaller than your smallest Lego.
One Lego shown as several pieces? Slide toward more. Two touching Legos shown as one? Slide toward less.

Pieces

No pieces yet.
How it tells pieces apart: it compares with the empty floor it saw first, so it can see even carpet-coloured bricks and ignores shadows. Different colours split by colour. Two same-colour bricks touching are split at the thin dark seam between them, or at the corner where they meet. Two bricks snapped together are one piece (the arm moves them together). Tap a piece for details.
